read1.reasoning: No complete English translation of the Opera exists in any register. The Calvin Translation Society (1843–55) covered most of the commentaries, and the Institutes, sermons and letters were translated separately. The modern-register translations are the Battles Institutes (1960), Torrance's New Testament commentaries (1959–72), and some sermons and other works. Together these are a substantial but incomplete part of the corpus. I ran one search and opened no pages, so URLs and quotes are only partly verified. A modern reader can read much of Calvin in English, but not the whole corpus.

The Calvin Translation Society commentaries are 19th-century, and the Torrance New Testament commentaries (1959 onward) are modern. The Battles Institutes (1960) is a complete modern translation of one work in the corpus, not of the whole collection.
